messages:
Maria G: Quick sync — I pushed a small spike for probabilistic sampling of token-level metering to reduce downstream cost. Need to align on auditability and where sampling should live (ingress vs runtime).
Jamal: numbers?
Maria G: Spike shows ~35% reduction in storage + downstream ops, ~2-3ms added on the critical path for deterministic hashing. But big question is: when we sample, do we lose the ability to resolve disputes or run post-hoc chargebacks?
Elena: Sampling will change per-tenant accuracy. If we go this route we need deterministic seeds per-tenant and a way to replay decisions for audits.
Rob: Agree. One approach: include sample_rate and sample_seed in the event envelope and make sampling deterministic (hash(tenant_id + request_id) < sample_rate). That lets us reproduce the sampled set if we still have the original payload in cold storage.
Sasha: Auditors and finance will push back unless enterprise tenants get full_fidelity. For legal chargebacks we need provable evidence.
Maria G: Proposal: hybrid model — full_fidelity for enterprise and sampled for self-serve. For sampled tenants, keep a write-ahead copy of the full payload to cheap S3 for 30–90 days; GC after that unless flagged by an audit.
Jamal: Implementation tradeoffs: if we sample at runtime (before enqueue), we save downstream CPU and storage. If we sample at ingest (after enqueue), we keep an immutable log but incur costs until compaction.
Rob: My preference: deterministic ingress sampling + write-ahead to low-cost object storage. Ingest marks event as sampled=true and publishes a compact envelope to Kafka. If audit needed, we fetch the original via fingerprint -> S3 path.
Elena: That pushes the interface boundary: what fields are in the compact envelope? We should standardize now.
Maria G: Minimal envelope draft — please review:

```
{
  "event_id": "uuid",
  "tenant_id": "team-123",
  "timestamp": "iso_ts",
  "sample_rate": "0.1",
  "sampled": true,
  "sample_seed": "0xdeadbeef",
  "fingerprint": "sha256(...)",
  "original_size": 4210,
  "ingest_node": "ingest-8",
  "provenance": "v1",
  "topics": ["metering.compact" ]
}
```

Rob: Add ingestion_ts and source_worker and keep a "payload_s3_path" optional field when we write the AW copy.
BillingBot: Deploy notice: sampling-config v1 rolled to canary (service: ingest, cfg: sampling_v1) :rocket:
Sasha: Main risk: disputes. Operational playbook: when a dispute is opened, we must be able to reconstruct the exact sampled decision and retrieve the original payload within 30 days. Otherwise finance loses.
Maria G: Action items: (1) write RFC that describes deterministic seed + envelope (Maria) (2) ingest change: sample+write-ahead + compact publish (Rob) (3) metrics: error bounds & reconciliation tests (Elena). Timeline: spike -> canary next week, 10% self-serve tenants.
Jamal: sgtm
Elena: I'll add validation tests for fingerprint collisions and sample reproducibility.
Rob: I'll prototype the write-ahead S3 layout and retention lifecycle; will include a cheap index (fingerprint -> s3 path) for quick retrieval.
Sasha: I'll run this by finance/legal for dispute acceptability; if they require longer retention for certain customers we'll just flag them as full_fidelity.
Maria G: Thanks all — I'll open the RFC and link the spike results. We'll use the canary traces to validate cost model and dispute latency. :thumbsup:
